messages:
sarah: Proposal — moving from hard rejects/long queues to a probabilistic degrade for saturated GPU pools. Instead of immediately rejecting when pool_util > threshold, we sample a fraction of incoming requests and apply a cheap-path (reduced max_tokens + quantized model routing). Goal: reduce hard failures and smooth p95 without exploding cost. Details below.

jason: What exact signals will drive the sampling? pool_util only? queue length? And do we have any estimate for p50/p95 change and cost delta?

sarah: Signals: pool_util, pending_queue_len, and region-network-loss. Trigger when pool_util >= 0.92 OR pending > 50. Sample rate defined as: sample_rate = clamp((pool_util - 0.9) * 2, 0, 0.2) + jitter. Degrade action: shrink max_tokens by 30% and route to model variant with quantized-profile `q4_fast` for that tenant. Fallback: if degraded request still exceeds latency SLO (p95 > 800ms) we fallback to immediate reject for that sticky bucket until next cool-down. Rough numbers from offline sim: when saturation hits, this reduces reject rate by ~60% and saves ~15-25% token-cost vs full queue expansion. Prototype config below: 

```json
{
  "admission_mode": "probabilistic_degrade",
  "triggers": {
    "pool_util_pct": 0.92,
    "pending_threshold": 50
  },
  "max_sample_rate": 0.2,
  "degrade_action": {
    "max_tokens_factor": 0.7,
    "model_variant": "q4_fast",
    "tag": "admit.degrade"
  },
  "fallback_latency_ms": 800,
  "sticky_window_sec": 300
}
```

nisha: Flagging a customer-consistency concern: degraded responses will vary in quality. We need per-tenant opt-out and a sticky assignment so a single user doesn't flip between full-quality and degraded on successive calls. Also add response header `X-RW-Degraded: true` so downstream shoppers and SDK can surface that. We must run a quality drift eval (sampled prompts + acceptance metrics) before Canary.

ops-bot: experiment created: id=exp-9123 name=admit-prob-degrade-2026-03-18 scope=overloaded-pools initial_traffic=5% owner=sarah

mike: Suggested rollback criteria: absolute error_rate increase > 0.5% and/or quality regression on blackbox eval > 2% absolute (depends on metric), or p95 latency increase > 50ms compared to baseline. Also require a dedicated alert `admit.degrade.usage > 0` and tracing tag 'admit.degrade' on requests so it shows up in flamegraphs.

emily: Implementation note: prefer a two-stage approach — short in-memory queue (max wait 100ms) then probabilistic degrade. That avoids long tail queue inversion. We should implement sample decision in the frontdoor (LB) so we don't pay RPC cost to route to GPU for requests we plan to degrade. Example pseudo: 

```text
if pool_util > trigger:
  if queue_wait_ms < 100:
    enqueue_short_queue()
  else:
    if random() < sample_rate:
      mark_request("degrade")
      route_to(q4_fast)
    else:
      reject_with(429)
```

sarah: Rollout plan: staging next Tue, Canary region-west-1 at 5% overloaded-pool traffic for 24h, then 20% for 6h, evaluate: degrade_rate, p50/p95 latency, token_cost_per_request, quality_eval_pass_rate. Dashboards: per-pool `degrade_rate`, `degrade_fallbacks`, `p95_latency`, `reject_rate`. Volunteers: @nisha will run eval harness, @jason will run admission-sim and infra rollout, @mike will own alerts and rollback hooks. If any alert fires, auto-disable experiment. :rocket:

jason: I'll run admission-sim across current fleet and post sim output (p95 delta, reject->degrade ratio, cost delta). Expect numbers tomorrow.

nisha: I'll prepare a seeded eval set with representative prompt buckets (chat, summarization, codegen) and mark threshold alerts. Will also add `X-RW-Degraded` propagation to SDK and docs.
